title: Strongly polynomial maximum flow below the \(mn\) barrier
formal: Do there exist a constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and a uniform randomized strongly polynomial algorithm that computes an exact maximum flow in every directed network with arbitrary nonnegative rational capacities, \(n\ge2\) vertices and \(m\ge n-1\) arcs, in \(O((mn)^{1-\varepsilon})\) worst-case arithmetic-RAM operations with success probability at least \(2/3\)?
definitions: The graph is given by its vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) arcs. It has no loops and at most one arc per ordered pair; opposite arcs are allowed. A feasible flow assigns a value \(f_{e}\) to every arc with \(0\le f_{e}\le u_{e}\) and equal incoming and outgoing total flow at each vertex except the distinct specified source \(s\) and sink \(t\). Its value is outgoing minus incoming flow at \(s\). The required output is a feasible flow attaining the largest possible value, including every arc value. Capacities and output values are finite rationals. Use exact rational cells with unit-cost copying, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by a nonzero rational and comparison. Integer control and addresses use \(O(\log(n+m+2))\)-bit words with unit-cost arithmetic, Boolean operations and shifts; they cannot inspect rational encodings or apply floor to rationals. Fixed rational constants and a fixed finite program are allowed, with no advice or free tables. Charge all arithmetic, control, memory access, random-word generation and output operations, treating each rational input or output as one cell. The count is independent of capacity magnitudes and binary lengths. For input bit length \(L\), every intermediate numerator and denominator and the total used bit space must be polynomially bounded in \(L\), including on unsuccessful executions. Independent fair random words are allowed. The bound holds on every execution; the entire flow must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). Constants and the polynomial bit-space bound are uniform over all instances.

context_blocks.text: Strongly polynomial flow bounds count arithmetic operations without making large numerical capacities a source of extra iterations. This distinguishes combinatorial network size from the bit complexity of the capacities.

Dadush, Orlin, Sidford and Végh explicitly ask for an \(O((mn)^{1-\varepsilon})\) strongly polynomial algorithm. Their SODA 2026 work improves structured networks while identifying \(O(mn)\) as the general bound.

Almost-linear algorithms for polynomially bounded integral capacities answer a different numerical-complexity question. Here one fixed exponent saving must hold for arbitrary rational capacities and every edge density.

why: A polynomial improvement over the general strongly polynomial maximum-flow barrier would separate a central combinatorial optimization primitive from its longstanding arithmetic complexity bound.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

sentences: Maximum flow asks for the greatest feasible transfer between a specified source and sink under arc capacities.
Here capacities are arbitrary nonnegative rationals.
The question asks for a fixed polynomial improvement over the general strongly polynomial arithmetic bound.
The operation count must be independent of capacity encodings while intermediate bit space remains polynomial.
Fast algorithms for bounded integral capacities and special graph classes do not establish this target.
